findings.title: The A18 transfer drill and its harness FAIL at D9 whenever the */15 approval.escalation_scan starter runs on the target between D7 and D9, so the A18 result depends on the wall clock; ADR-0064 A3.9 residual 1 was never decided and is not disclosed in any handover text or A18 register row
findings.reproduction: Disposable shared clone at 02aeed6e (candidate sha256:07af9fba26f9ae435f6f3de7ca5204ed1e182a125f1fd0f912b70da06035a61d), Node 24.21.0, tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh. (1) Natural occurrence: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/qa/round-5/a18/qa-r5-a18-driver.sh (the round-4 driver with the new candidate id) built a fresh archive; part 1 (transfer-drill.sh --keep) PASSED with D9 at 07:10:32Z; part 2, the shipped harness tests/qa/integration/a18-transfer-drill.test.ts with QA_A18_REQUIRE=1 on the same archive, FAILED 4 of 10 tests: the drill's D9 restart happened just after 07:15:00Z and mode 2 reported 'automation_execution: 17 added ... unexplained added [01a1e336-6adf-7a11-af63-c8f6347fcaf8]' and the same for automation_action_result, then 'D9 FAIL, D10 NOT_RUN, D11 NOT_RUN'. Only that run's worker handled approval.escalation_scan after the restart. (2) Control: the harness alone re-run at 07:20 (D7-D9 at about 07:24-07:25Z) passed 10/10 with 16 executions, all explained. (3) Deliberate reproduction on the unmodified candidate: qa-r5-d9-boundary-repro.sh with QA_START=07:56:05 runs deploy/scripts/transfer-drill.sh --keep so that D7-D9 contains 08:00:00Z. The drill exits 1 with D9 FAIL. The kept target database holds exactly one schedule-triggered execution, 01a1e35f-8e4f-7de0-80d2-0aab0e420e27, trigger_code approval.escalation_scan, trigger_key approval.escalation_scan:2026-11-16T08:00, created 08:00:52.8Z, initiating_user_id NULL, and its starter_handler result 01a1e35f-8e85-72b8-bcd3-074233427210. job_schedule: approval.escalation_scan '*/15 * * * *' Asia/Riyadh; apps/worker/src/automation/starters.ts maps the queue to starter.decision_sla. An attempt aimed at 07:45 missed the slot by 3 s and passed.
findings.expected: REQ-S19-017 (A18): 'the drill report shows matching counts and checksums, working evidence downloads under the new base URL, successful key workflows, and records, jobs and approvals intact after a full restart'. The shipped drill is the operator's and the reviewer's proof of that clause (docs/handover/deployment.md, the A18 harness). Run against a correct installation, it should give the same result whatever the time of day. If a known residual can make it fail, ADR-0064 A3.9 residual 1 says 'the orchestrator decides': I expect either that decision (and a drill or explaining-rule change), or at least a disclosure that tells the operator a scheduled starter in the D7-D9 window gives a D9 FAIL that is not a data defect.
findings.actual: The result depends on the wall clock. 2 of my 5 D9 runs on this candidate failed: the run-1 harness at 07:15 and the reproduction at 08:00. 3 passed: the run-1 direct drill, the run-2 harness and reproduction attempt 1; none of their windows contained a quarter hour. The product itself is correct: a scheduled job runs after the restart and writes its execution and audit event. The mode 2 recheck classifies schedule-triggered executions as unexplained by design (A3.9). With the worker up for about 46-60 s from D7 to D9 and approval.escalation_scan every 15 minutes, about 5-7 % of runs fail on time alone. The daily starters between 00:05 and 00:45 Asia/Riyadh add more. DO-D4 measured none (T-B17), so the residual was never hit before, and no decision was recorded. It is absent from known-limitations.md, the release notes, deployment.md and the notes of REQ-S19-017, REQ-S20-018 and REQ-S01-006 (grep and python3 in d9-schedule-window-analysis.log §7). An operator or a later reviewer who runs the shipped drill near a quarter hour gets an A18 FAIL with no documented explanation. Medium (D-192): this is a real defect in the acceptance drill with a bounded effect. No data is wrong and no authorization is affected, so it is not mandatory. It must be repaired before the gate: the orchestrator decides A3.9, then the explaining rule or the drill changes, or the residual is disclosed with the operator's recovery (re-run outside the slot). The ADR forbids pausing or rescheduling the job to avoid it.

history.note: Raised by qa-verifier in DG7 round 5 on candidate sha256:07af9fba26f9ae435f6f3de7ca5204ed1e182a125f1fd0f912b70da06035a61d.
